rv.q: But in the end, this is a show about songs. And I’ve seen Theo Ubique do far better.

Theo Ubique's The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas is a rollicking good time filled with political upheaval, heartfelt moments, and some of the best choreography I've seen in community theatre to-date (major kudos to choreographer Jenna Schoppe).
It’s impossible to forget, much like Theo Ubique Theatre’s entire wonderful, effervescent, toe-tapping production.
This might just be the subtle takeaway from Theo Ubique Cabaret Theatre’s endearing, only slightly bawdy, overall splendid production of the seldom-produced The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas .
For an evening of rollicking fun, this production has it all.
For those looking for an upbeat night out at a fun musical, this would be a good fit for you.
To get a little perspective, everyone deserves to take a trip to “The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas.”
The production has some kinks to iron out but, nevertheless, is a great showcase of Carol Hall’s beautiful songs and Larry L. King and Peter Masterson’s bittersweet and caustic book.
The cabaret setting makes it a fun way to spend the evening.
Under the sharp direction of Landree Fleming and choreographer Jenna Schoppe, they have created a sharp, quick paced version of the show...
